bullets.title: Risk-off since Nov 5 Blue Sweep; Fed still hiking with core PCE at 3.26%
bullets.body: UBS flags a risk-off episode that began Nov 5, 2026 following the Blue Sweep announcement and an escalating US-Iran conflict. Core PCE sits at 3.26% YoY and is expected to tick up to 3.34% in November before gradually declining; UBS expects the Fed to deliver two more hikes, with US yields likely range-bound. Despite a -4 z-score daily equity return drop, investors remain reluctant to price systemic instability.

bullets.title: AI capex slowdown priced even as demand accelerates; policy constraints may cap supply
bullets.body: UBS notes that markets have already priced an AI capex slowdown despite underlying AI demand continuing to accelerate. Policy constraints are seen as a potential limiter on new supply additions, keeping the demand/supply imbalance in place. Global defense and AI-related spending expected to remain elevated into 2027.

bullets.title: TEPCO to invest $64B in AI power infrastructure through 2030, targeting AWS and hyperscalers
bullets.body: TEPCO plans to invest JPY10.2T (~$64B) in power grids and nuclear plants through FY30 to serve US hyperscaler data centers, with Amazon Web Services cited as a prospective customer. The utility plans to ramp data center power supply 8x by FY25 and 16x by FY40, targeting EBITDA (after decommissioning costs) of JPY1.4T in FY35 vs. JPY722.3B projected for FY27. TEPCO is in capital alliance talks with SoftBank, KKR, Blackstone, and Global Infrastructure Partners.

bullets.title: Brazil macro deteriorating: 0.6% growth in 2027, Selic at 13.75%, debt rising to 88% GDP
bullets.body: JPMorgan sees Brazil slowing sharply to 0.6% GDP growth in 2027 with recession a real risk, as heavy debt-service burdens and tight credit conditions weigh on activity. Inflation is projected to rise to ~6% in early 2027 before easing to 5.5% year-end, still well above the 3% target, keeping the Selic at 13.75%. Public debt is forecast to climb from 84% of GDP in 2026 to 92% by 2028, with a loss of confidence the key tail risk.

bullets.title: Mexico BoP: Record tech exports drive CA surplus, but IG downgrade risk and portfolio outflows loom
bullets.body: Mexico posted a 0.21% of GDP current account surplus in 3Q26—its second-highest for any third quarter—on record goods exports of $237.5bn (up 40.6% YoY), driven by the tech boom. However, portfolio investment outflows totaled $5.8bn as foreign investors reduced exposure, the peso has weakened more than 8% since end-3Q26, and S&P is expected to downgrade Mexico to one notch above high-yield within 12 months (Fitch and Moody's already there).

bullets.title: Argentina: JPM OW but election risk dominates; sovereign spread above 1,100bp
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintains an Overweight on Argentina but flags the October 2027 presidential election as the critical test for fiscal and pro-investment policy continuity. Markets are pricing roughly 50% probability of a regime change, with sovereign spreads widening above 1,100bp. Under the base case, GDP grows 0.8% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, with exports rising to $100.8bn in 2026 and 21.6% growth in 2027 as Vaca Muerta energy and mining projects ramp.
